newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian ministry approves opposition protest.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian ministry approves opposition protest.

text.p: Cambodia's Interior Ministry on Tuesday approved an opposition request to rally against the arrest of one of its senior members on murder charges but forbade the demonstrators from marching.
"The ministry agreed but asked for a peaceful protest without marching on public streets," ministry spokesman Sok Phal said.

The Khmer Nation Party (KNP) last weekend requested permission for a protest march on Wednesday outside the detention centre where the party's security chief and steering committee member Srun Vong Vannak was being held.
The officially unrecognised KNP has said the detention was illegal and it planned the protest to demand his release.

Srun Vong Vannak and two other men were charged last week with involvement in the November 19 murder of co-Premier Hun Sen's brother-in-law outside a Phnom Penh restaurant. KNP leader Sam Rainsy said on Tuesday he might call off the march if the authorities agreed to allow Srun Vong Vannak access to a lawyer for the first time since his February 14 arrest.

He said if the demand was not granted before the planned start of Wednesday's march, the KNP would ignore the ministry's order to confine its protest to just outside party headquarters and would march to the detention centre.
Sam Rainsy wrote to King Norodom Sihanouk on Monday appealing for a royal order to grant Srun Vong Vannak access to legal counsel. The king's answer was not known.
The outspoken opposition leader claims his security chief's arrest was engineered by his bitter foe Hun Sen in a bid to destabilise the KNP.
The KNP recently formed an alliance with the royalist FUNCINPEC party, main partner and rival of Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party in the uneasy coalition government formed in 1993.
